content.title: Carvana, Robinhood, Coinbase: The 3 biggest turnarounds from 2022
content.description:
Carvana (CVNA), Robinhood Markets (HOOD), and Coinbase Global (COIN) have two main themes in common as 2025 draws to a close: all three are the latest additions to the S&P 500 (^GSPC) this year, and they were the biggest market losers in 2022. Carvana will be joining the market index on Monday, December 22.

Yahoo Finance senior markets reporter Ines Ferré outlines each of the three companies' most pivotal moments in their turnarounds from 2022 lows.

content.title: Carvana Shares Hit Record Ahead of S&P 500 Inclusion
content.summary: Carvana reported surprisingly strong quarterly sales in November, and the Dec. 5 announcement that it would be added to the S&P 500 index further fueled its gains.  The company, which debuted on the stock market in 2017, offers a primarily online experience and at-home exchanges of new vehicles and trade-ins.  Only a few years ago, investors seemed unsure Carvana would survive.

content.title: Carvana Notches $33 Billion, 12-Day Run Ahead of S&P Entry
content.summary: The shares of Carvana, which went public in 2017, climbed over 50% from Nov. 21 close, the session before the run of gains began, and have added over $33 billion to the valuation over that stretch.  The S&P 500 entry, announced Dec. 5, has added fuel to the shares’ ascent.  S&P Dow Jones Indices said Carvana will join along with CRH Plc and Comfort Systems USA Inc. The first day Carvana trades in the index will be Dec. 22.

content.title: Carvana Stock Is on a Winning Streak Like None It’s Ever Seen. It’s Up 50% in 12 Days.
content.summary: Carvana  has been on a tear this year after shaking off allegations that its turnaround was a “mirage.” Now, the stock is set to notch a new record.  Shares of the used-car dealer rose 1.1% to $461.40 on Wednesday, putting them on pace for the longest winning streak in  Carvana’s  history as a public company.  If the gains hold and the stock closes above $459.68, the company’s market capitalization will surpass the $100 billion threshold for the first time on record.
